STRATEGY: Parent starts C, retaliates against last-round defection, and randomly probes with D when cooperation ratio is high. Trace simulates peers/archive, including slot 7's forgiveness and TFT-style retaliation, and designs a one-time early probe followed by TFT/forgiveness. Proposed change: probe once, stop probing if opponent retaliates, and otherwise exploit forgiving/always-C opponents.

STRATEGY: Parent slot 8 is described as probing randomly (15% chance every 17 rounds when coop_ratio >=0.85) and scoring lower; the trace simulates probing/exploiting against forgiving peers (slot 0, slot 7) and TFT, then designs a one-time probe at round 5 if all history is CC, switching to forgiving TFT after retaliation.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the best is to mimic the top strategies but add a safe exploit. Let's look at the top strategy slot 7."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like policy (slot 7) that retaliates after opponent defection and forgives with some probability. The trace simulates interactions with slot 0, TFT, always-D, and always-C opponents, then designs a hybrid: exploit mode (defect while no DD has occurred and opponent keeps cooperating) wrapped around the slot 7 base logic, plus an always-defector detection rule.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Thus, this hybrid strategy should outperform the parent and likely slot 7. Let's write the final code cleanly."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-style policy with stochastic forgiveness and anti-always-defect detection. The trace simulates an exploit wrapper that cooperates until round 5, then defects while the opponent has never defected, falling back to base logic once either side defects. It changes the exploit condition to require opp_def == 0 and rewrites the final strategy accordingly.
